newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-NICHOLAS LEADS AFTER SECOND ROUND OF U.S. WOMEN'S OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NICHOLAS LEADS AFTER SECOND ROUND OF U.S. WOMEN'S OPEN.

text.p: Englishwoman Alison Nicholas is not a morning person, but she rubbed the sleep from her eyes in time to take the second-round lead at the U.S. Women's Open Friday.
Nicholas, who was up at 5 a.m. to prepare for her 7.18 a.m. tee time, reeled off five birdies in a five-under-par 66 at Pumpkin Ridge.
It not only was equal to the day's lowest round, but was her best score in 28 rounds at the U.S. Women's Open.
The 35-year-old golfer posted a six-under 136 halfway total to stand one stroke ahead of Swede Liselotte Neumann (70) and Americans Nancy Lopez (68) and Kelly Robbins (69).
The cut fell at five-over 147, and the most notable casualty was two-time defending champion Annika Sorenstam.
"I'm not good in the mornings," said Nicholas, who has won twice on the LPGA Tour and 12 times on the European Women's Tour, including the 1987 British Open.

"I was very quiet for about an hour after I got up because I couldn't cope with talking to anyone, but I hit it well on the range and I was ready to play. Without any bogeys, that's one of my best rounds."
She has been in good form in Europe recently, as she showed by reaching a playoff at the Evian Masters last month.
Neumann, meanwhile, birdied four of the first seven holes to go eight under, but she surrendered her advantage with bogeys at the final three holes.
"The first 15 holes I hit the ball great," said Neumann, the 1988 champion. "Everything was working my way but I hooked my drive on 16 and got really uncomfortable after that.
"I'm sure there was a little bit of nervousness coming into the last couple of holes. I know how important this event is. I know what it takes to win."
Lopez, in contrast to Neumann, birdied the final three holes to move within sight of a long overdue victory in the most important championship in women's golf.

"My game is the best it's been at a U.S. Open for a while," said Lopez, 40, who has finished second three times. Her best chance came in 1977, where she struggled to concentrate after the zipper in her shorts broke during the final round.
"I couldn't keep my mind off my zipper, couldn't focus on what was going on," Lopez recalled.
While the leaders prepared for the weekend, Sorenstam packed her bags after her quest to win the championship an unprecedented three years in a row came to a rapid halt.
"I really don't know what's wrong. I'm going to go home and replay the holes in my head and figure out what's wrong," said the Swede, who shot 73 for 150.

She had made 61 consecutive cuts in an impressive streak going back three years, and she still had a chance of making it 62 until she took a double bogey at the par-four 13th, where her seven-iron cleared the green and bounced into a hazard.
Other notables with the weekend off included England's Laura Davies, who double-bogeyed the final hole to miss out by one stroke, and last year's runner-up, Kris Tschetter.
